q: 301. Higher workability of concrete is required if the structure is
explain: In thick, heavily reinforced sections the congestion of steel restricts free movement of concrete, so a higher workability mix is needed to ensure the concrete flows around bars and fills every corner without honeycombing.

q: 302. Pick up the correct statement form the following:
options: higher workability indicates unexpected increase in the moisture content
higher workability indicates deficiency of sand
if the concrete mix is dry, the slump is zero
concrete mix having zero slump is unsuitable for high strength
explain: All the listed statements are individually true observations relating slump/workability to moisture, sand content and mix dryness, so 'all of the above' is correct.

q: 303. The maximum thickness of concrete floor of a cement warehouse, is
explain: A cement warehouse floor carries heavy stacked loads, so codes specify a relatively thick slab, with 25 cm being the maximum recommended thickness for such floors.

q: 304. The shuttering of a hall measuring 4 m x 5 m, can be removed after
explain: For slabs/beams with spans greater than 4.5 m (props under beams/slabs spanning more than about 4.5 m), formwork should remain in place for 14 days as per standard formwork removal periods.

q: 305. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: there should not be any loss of cement from the charged drum of the mixer
cement should be mixed for at least one minute
10% of water is placed in the rotating drum before adding dry material
10% of water is added after placing the other ingredients in the drum
explain: All these are standard good-practice requirements for charging and mixing a concrete mixer, so the combined statement 'all of the above' is correct.

q: 306. If the effective working time is 7 hours and per batch time of concrete mixer of 150 litre capacity, is
explain: Multiplying the number of batches that can be produced by a 150-litre mixer within the effective 7-hour working period (based on a typical batch cycle time) gives a total output of about 18,900 litres of concrete.

q: 307. The main object of compaction of concrete is
options: to provide intimate contact between the concrete and embedded materials
explain: Compaction removes entrapped air, densifies the mix, and ensures concrete is in intimate contact with reinforcement/embedded parts — all these are objectives of compaction.

q: 308. Non-uniform compaction may cause the concrete
explain: Uneven compaction leaves pockets of poorly consolidated concrete, making it porous, non-homogeneous, and weaker in strength — hence all effects occur together.

q: 309. The compaction of concrete, improves
explain: Proper compaction expels air voids, which simultaneously increases density, strength, and durability of the hardened concrete.

q: 310. The final operation of finishing floors, is known
explain: Trowelling is carried out last, after floating, to produce a smooth, dense, and hard surface finish on concrete floors.

q: 311. The operation of removing humps and hollows of uniform concrete surface, is known as
explain: Screeding is the process of striking off excess concrete with a straightedge to remove humps and hollows and bring the surface to the required level.

q: 312. The ratio of the length and breadth of wooden float, is
explain: A wooden float used for finishing concrete surfaces typically has a length-to-breadth ratio of about 7.5, giving a long narrow tool for smoothing the surface.

q: 313. Construction joints are provided
options: where BM and SF are small
where it is supported by another member
at 18 m apart in huge structures
in concrete wall at sill level of windows
explain: Construction joints are located at points of low bending moment/shear, at supports, at regular intervals in large structures, and at window sill levels in walls — all of these are valid locations.

q: 314. The surface where two successive placements of concrete meet, is known as
explain: A construction joint is, by definition, the interface formed where one concreting operation stops and the next placement begins.

q: 315. A construction joint is provided where
options: it is supported by other member
explain: Construction joints are best located where internal forces (BM and SF) are minimal or where the member is supported, so all the listed conditions are appropriate locations.

q: 316. Horizontal construction joins in concrete walls are generally provided at
explain: Horizontal construction joints in walls are conventionally placed at soffit level, window sill level, and floor level, since these are natural break points in the pour.

q: 317. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: construction joints in columns are provided a few cm below the junction of beam
construction joints in columns are provided at the bottom haunching
construction joints in beam and slabs are provided within middle third
construction joints are generally provided in positions subjected to least shear force
explain: Each statement correctly describes accepted practice for locating construction joints in columns, beams and slabs, so the combined answer 'all of the above' applies.

q: 318. Joints in concrete structures, are provided
options: to reduce the tensile stresses likely to be developed due to evaporation of water
to minimize the change in the dimensions of the slab
explain: Joints in concrete relieve tensile stresses from shrinkage/temperature effects, limit dimensional change, and control cracking, so all listed purposes are correct.

q: 319. Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structures exceeds
explain: Expansion joints are generally introduced in long concrete structures once their length exceeds about 40 m, to accommodate thermal movement.

q: 320. According to the recommendations of IS:456-2000, expansion joints
options: are provided where plane changes abruptly
are provided to ensure minimum resistance
do not carry reinforcement across them
explain: IS:456-2000 recommends expansion joints at abrupt plan changes, designed to offer minimum resistance to movement, supported independently, and without reinforcement crossing them — all points are valid.

q: 321. Construction joints are generally provided in concrete
explain: Construction joints are a common feature in roads, retaining walls, channel linings, and tunnel linings wherever concreting must be carried out in separate stages.

q: 322. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: construction joins are necessarily planned for their locations
expansion joints are provided to accommodate thermal expansion
construction joints are provided to control shrinkage cracks
expansion joints need not be provided in foundation concrete
explain: Each statement is a correct principle about joint design and location, so together they form the correct combined answer.

q: 323. The main purpose of concrete design mix is
options: mixing the concrete in better way
explain: Design mixing proportions the ingredients scientifically to achieve the required strength and durability at the most economical cement content, making cost economy its main purpose.

q: 324. Generally nominal mix is done by volume while design mix is done by
explain: Design mixes require accurate proportioning of ingredients, which is achieved by batching materials by weight rather than the less precise volume batching used in nominal mixes.

q: 325. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the free water is the amount of water added while mixing and the amount of water held on the surface of the aggregates prior to mixing
the total water is the free water and the amount actually absorbed by the aggregates
explain: Free water and total water are defined the opposite way to how they are stated here — free water excludes surface moisture already on the aggregate before mixing, so neither statement is technically correct as worded.

q: 326. If the average compressive strength is 4000 kg/cm2 and standard deviation is 500, the coefficient of variation is
explain: Coefficient of variation = (standard deviation / mean) x 100 = (500/4000) x 100 = 12.5%.

q: 327. The risk of segregation is more for
explain: Wetter mixes, a larger proportion of maximum-size aggregate, and coarser grading all reduce cohesion of the mix, increasing the likelihood that coarse aggregate separates from the mortar (segregation).

q: 328. The process by which fresh cement concrete is compacted to remove the air bubbles is known as
explain: Compaction is the specific operation of expelling entrapped air from freshly placed concrete, typically by vibration or ramming.

q: 329. Maturity of concrete means
options: sum of product of temperature & time
explain: Maturity is a concept that combines the effects of curing temperature and time (the temperature-time factor), used to estimate strength gain, rather than simply age.

q: 330. Gypsum is used as admixture in concrete to increase the property of concrete
explain: Gypsum is interground with clinker/added to cement primarily to retard/regulate the initial setting time, acting as a retarder.

q: 331. Calcium chloride is used as admixture in concrete to increase the property of concrete
explain: Calcium chloride is a well-known chemical accelerator that speeds up the hydration process and early strength gain of concrete.

q: 332. Calcium chloride as an accelerating admixture is not recommended for use with
explain: With high alumina cement, calcium chloride can cause flash setting and a serious loss of ultimate strength, so its use is specifically avoided in that case.

q: 333. To improve the certain properties of concrete, admixture is used at the time of
explain: Admixtures are dosed into the mix during the mixing stage so that they are uniformly dispersed and can act effectively throughout the concrete.

q: 334. An admixture
options: is a basic ingredient of concrete
offers improvement not economically attained by adjusting mix proportions
is a substitute for good concreting practice
is beneficial to the properties of concrete when used in large quantities
explain: An admixture is defined as a material used to achieve special properties (workability, setting time, etc.) that could not be economically obtained just by varying the basic mix proportions.

q: 335. An admixture could be used to
explain: Different classes of admixtures can accelerate setting, enhance strength, or improve workability, so admixtures collectively serve all these purposes.

q: 336. An accelerator shortens all of the following except
explain: An accelerator speeds up setting, curing duration, and permits earlier formwork removal, but it does not 'shorten' strength — strength is a magnitude, not a time-based quantity, so it is the exception.

q: 337. Addition of retarder to concrete decreases all of the following except
explain: A retarder slows the rate of hydration and rate of strength development, but it does not necessarily decrease workability (in fact it can be prolonged) or ultimate compressive strength, making this option the exception.

q: 338. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
explain: Since different types of admixtures individually achieve acceleration of hydration, waterproofing, acid resistance and strength gain, none of the listed statements is incorrect on its own.

q: 339. Gel space ratio is defined as the ratio of
options: volume of hydrated cement to the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores
the sum of volume of hydrated cement and capillary pores to volume of hydrated cement
both a) and b) of above
explain: Gel-space ratio is defined by Powers as the volume of the gel (hydration products) divided by the sum of the volume of the gel and the capillary pore space it occupies.

q: 340. Find the gel space ratio of concrete with following data: cement = 50 kg, Weight of water = 20 kg
explain: Substituting the given cement and water quantities into the standard gel-space ratio formula (relating the volume of hydration products to total space occupied) gives a ratio of approximately 0.91.

q: 341. The minimum grade of high strength concrete is
explain: High strength concrete is classified as concrete with a characteristic strength of M60 grade and above.

q: 342. The type of aggregates not suitable for high strength concrete and for pavements subjected to tension, is
explain: Rounded aggregates give poor interlocking and lower bond strength with cement paste, making them unsuitable where high strength and good tensile/flexural performance (as in pavements) are needed.

q: 343. The aggregate used for high strength concrete is
explain: Angular aggregate provides strong mechanical interlocking and better bond with the cement paste, which is essential for achieving high strength concrete.

q: 344. To obtain a very high strength concrete, use very fine grained
explain: Very fine grained granite aggregate/powder is used to densify the microstructure and achieve very high compressive strength in specialty concrete mixes.

q: 345. Prestress is imparted to concrete by bearing in
explain: In post-tensioning, the prestressing force is transferred to the concrete through end anchorages bearing against the concrete member, unlike pre-tensioning where it is transferred by bond.

q: 346. The minimum grade of concrete for pre-tensioned member is
explain: Pre-tensioned members require high early strength to allow release of the tendons, so a minimum grade of M40 concrete is specified.

q: 347. The mix proportion of cement mortar to be used in the joints in precast prestressed member is
explain: A relatively rich mortar mix of 1:1.5 (cement:sand) is recommended for filling joints between precast prestressed concrete units to ensure adequate strength and durability.

q: 348. The diameter of high tensile steel tendons used is
explain: High tensile steel wires used as tendons in prestressed concrete typically range from about 5 mm to 8 mm in diameter.

q: 349. The minimum clear spacing for single wires used in pre-tension system is
options: 2 times the diameter of the wire and max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
3 times the diameter of the wire and max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
2 times the diameter of the wire and 1.5 times max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
3 times the diameter of the wire and 1.5 times max. size of aggregate whichever is greater
explain: IS code requires the minimum clear spacing between single pre-tensioned wires to be the greater of 3 times the wire diameter or 1.5 times the maximum aggregate size, to ensure proper compaction and bond.

q: 350. The minimum clear spacing of non-grouped cables or large bars shall be
options: maximum size of cable or bar
5 mm plus maximum size of aggregate
explain: The code specifies the minimum clear spacing for non-grouped cables/large bars as whichever is greatest among 40 mm, the cable/bar size, or 5 mm plus the maximum aggregate size.
